title: Bring the Gavel Down
subtitle: Boundaries are intangible, existing within the depths of every heart.

trails.title: Storm Syndrome Investigation Record
trails.description: A hastily made report about the first great war painting of the century.

content.text:
The symptoms of the current Storm Syndrome can be roughly summarized as oil painting transformation and heightened delirium. Depending on the region, the severity of the Storm Syndrome also varies:

Vienna

Expressionistic oil painting transformation pervades the body uncontrollably. At the same time, emotional stability is severely impaired—irritability and abnormal behavior occur, including but not limited to:


• Using deadly force to correct pronunciation.¹

• Declaring oneself as an independent nation and founding a country by family unit.

• Identifying parties by the color of their oil paintings and persecuting people of different colors.

...

Athens

Oil painting transformation symptoms only appear on the face, with a few cases of recovery reported, specific reasons unknown. Aggressiveness increases, especially a strong destructive impulse toward olive trees.²

Democratic votes on whether to go to war have occurred several times in different squares, often splitting into two factions and starting a war during the vote.

Cairo

Oil painting transformation symptoms are limited to parts of the facial organs, with minor actual effects on the body, which can largely be ignored. The main mental effect is reflected in an increase in swearing.

The local military, severely affected, has begun attempting to convert the pyramids into war fortifications.

...

...

...

Based on feedback from investigators around the world, it has been tentatively concluded that the epicenter of this "Storm" is Vienna, and the closer the physical distance to the epicenter, the more severe the symptoms of the Storm Syndrome.

¹Example: German speakers with non-Austrian accents have been attacked by Austrians.

²To be more precise, this is an act of rebellion against peace.

items.text: Bring the Gavel Down

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: Ms. Vertin, did you just say the "Emanation" has happened?

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: Just now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: More precisely, its 24-hour countdown has begun.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's always a buffer period before the "Storm," during which the Storm Syndrome gradually spreads from the Critical Point across the globe. The symptoms are different every time, and we have yet to discern a pattern.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: With the help of Laplace Scientific Computing Center, the best we can do now is to send a 24-hour warning prior to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Another minute has passed.
The hall is once again filled with the whispers of the white robes.
On this island dedicated solely to the study of the "Emanation," the situation has far surpassed their imaginations.
Please remain seated, everyone. We are still in the middle of a vote!
The "Emanation" holds no influence on this island. The discussion must continue until a satisfactory conclusion is reached. No other subjects shall be brought up until then.
The banshee, acting as Custodian of the assembly, raises her voice, drowning out the arguments.
Despite the unforeseen turn of events, she remains committed to her duty—the debate must go on.
Come here, 37. Can someone please bring her a blanket?
Her voice softens as she looks at the frail, slender girl in front of her.
42, go with Sophia and check on those Abraxases.
The man bows and leaves.
Order is restored under the dome once more.
Ah, good news, good news indeed!
We are freed from the pain of choosing whom to blame, are we not?
What?
The rhetorician raises a hand with a triumphant smile.
As usual, he's offering a new perspective, or what some might call another attempt at stirring up the crowd.
The "Emanation" is coming. The tides of pneuma will pour from above and wash away all trivialities.
By then, human intruders and the international powers of this era, along with the turmoil they brought,
will all be dissolved and poured into the ditches like gunk.
And we will regain our shores and return to the study of essence and Forms.
His words are met with silence.
The crowd is lost in thought. Having long detached themselves from the phenomenal world, 210's words are striking a chord.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No, it's different this time!
The petite figure stands on her feet.
She is pale as snow from her coma, and did not bother to put on the blanket given to her.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The island has fallen ill!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's getting bloated, stagnant, and sluggish, drifting into the World of Matters where ignorance reigns.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Soon, the tides of pneuma will wash over us, sweeping away the fragments of the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: What did you say?!

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: In other words, we will all be taken by the "Emanation"? This ...

items.speaker: Believer V
items.text: This is unthinkable!
This is terrible news, one that nobody wants to hear right now.
The impact is like a bomb going off, the crowd is buzzing with fearful whispers.
The lady next to 37 stands up, still holding the unused blanket.

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: 37, you just woke up from a coma. You're not well.

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: Why don't you take another rest?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No, no time for that. I'm here to warn you.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Apeiron is gone. I can no longer sense It. This has never happened before!
Why are you so surprised, 37?
The question is asked softly, but it cuts like ice.
You should know the reason of Its alienation.
You brought outsiders to the sacred place. You betrayed the Scriptures' teachings and angered Apeiron!
Of course, I may have jumped to this accusation, as Manus Vindictae also intruded our sacred place without permission.
People! As of now, there's no proof that the "Emanation" will influence the island. 37's account is lacking.
And we are still plagued by suspicions, accusations, and the damages done to our home.
We are to proceed with the hearing and reach a final verdict on both the Foundation and Manus Vindictae.
The attempt to refocus the assembly fails as half the audience turns their attention to the gate.
Sophia has returned, standing hesitantly in front of the entrance.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm sorry. Please forgive me. I shouldn't have intruded the Hall of Truth, but ...
Though irritated by the constant interruptions, the Custodian immediately notices her peculiar expression.
Sophia, weren't you and 42 checking on the Abraxases?
What is the matter?
The Corrector gestures in the air, her voice shaking.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The Abraxases don't look right! Their beaks, no, their entire heads are melting into oil paints.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: And 42 ... We were on the beach, suddenly, he ...
Her words trail off.
Beyond the open gate, the screeching of the bird monsters completes her sentence.
The other believer appears behind her, shoving Sophia aside as he flails and stumbles into the hall. His face is melting, colorful oil paints forming a puddle on the floor.

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: Hahaha! Now I see, it finally all makes sense!

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: There never was the Truth, nor the transcendental! Everything is a lie! Nothing but shadows on walls, flickers of fire, and fragments of reality!

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: No one will survive the oblivion! The island will be destroyed amid its conflict!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is that the Storm Syndrome?
42, your face ...
Completely disregarding those around him, he bursts into maniacal laughter, casting an arcane glow in his palms.
He jumps onto a seat and knocks over a row of torches.

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: NO ONE!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 888, stop conversing with him!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We must subdue him, now!
The Hall of Apeiron

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He has the Storm Syndrome!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, listen, everyone. 37 is right. Something's changed on this island. Your immunity to the "Emanation" has been weakened!
42 lies motionless on the floor, his face still a mess of colorful paint.
Fear and uncertainty quickly arise around him.

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: How? That's never happened in the last eight times!
A feeble induction, my friend. Just because you've never seen a purple cow, doesn't mean it doesn't exist.

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: Must we talk of logic now?! 42 has literally been "emanated"!

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: First the army, then the "Emanation." Everything's been falling apart since the outsiders arrived on this island.

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: The Foundation and Manus Vindictae—one of them must answer for this.

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: Then you should also ask 37 and number "0" what they've done in the sacred place to anger Apeiron so much!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, 37 didn't cause this. I told you. It was Manus Vindictae!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They broke the peace agreement and launched suicide attacks. They forced their way into the cave.

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: You and them are equally responsible on this matter!

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: They at least paid with their lives. What about you?

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: You claim that 42's abnormality was caused by the "Emanation," but how are we to believe that it isn't, in fact, the work of your arcane skills?

items.speaker: Believer IV
items.text: As we went through your belongings, Ms. Vertin, we found a golden sampling device. Enlighten us: What exactly is the Foundation looking for here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's ...

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Heh-heh.
From the other side of the hall comes a soft chuckle.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Good, Vertin. Good.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Let the confrontations be louder and the struggles be harder.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I wonder what shall come of this.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Silence!
The gavel slams down with a heavy, undeniable thud.
The host of the assembly rises to his feet, his face unusually grave.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The debate will end now.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Since we were unable to come to an agreement, further discussion is pointless. There are more pressing matters to attend to.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: This will be the end of the assembly, and my decision will be the final ruling:

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I demand that both parties leave this island at once.
The decision is clear and final.
As the number of reconciliation, 6 has been mindful of his use of unilateral authority.
Yet, there are no objections this time.
The hall falls into a silence—a silence that demands a decision.
What to do?
Wait for Arcana's move.

branch.text: Leaving the island would be a huge loss. The discussion about the "Storm" has only just begun, and the depths of the cave is yet to be explored.
Worst of all, the leader of Manus Vindictae—she can't be left here with the School of Apeiron.
Will she accept the verdict? Will she appeal?
Just what exactly is she after?
It's a zero-sum game, where the first one to react is more likely to lose.
The best course of action is to wait.

branch.speaker: Arcana
branch.text: The decisions of my fellow brethren shall be respected.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: I also agree with your verdict.

items.text: Accept 6's verdict.

branch.text: The outcome is still acceptable, things will just go back to square one.
Besides, the concepts exchanged on the "Storm" and the samples of asymmetrical nuclide R are already significant advancements for subsequent research.
More importantly, if the School of Apeiron cannot form an alliance with the Foundation, they must be stopped from joining forces with the enemy instead.
This is a chance to take the initiative and avoid being caught in a reactive position.
All that's needed is to stand up and nod.
Now comes the real issue—what will she choose to do?

branch.speaker: Arcana
branch.text: My choice matches that of Vertin's.

items.text: She casually agrees, just as she did when asked to pledge on the stone bangles.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: But may I ask for one small doubt to be dispelled?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Ms. Vertin and I will depart ere long. Do you truly not desirest aid from us?

items.speaker: Six
items.text: You're kind to ask, miss.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It is true that our circle has been disturbed, but we see it as a mere turbulence of the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: He who holds the compass decides the circle. This will not shift the center of our focus, nor change the shape of our beliefs.
6 bends down, laying his hand on 42's forehead.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Μηδὲν ἄγαν.

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: *breathes peacefully*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He purged the Storm Syndrome with an arcane skill?!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I never thought it'd be possible.
The leader straightens up, looking as composed as ever.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The light of intelligence has cleansed 42 of confusion. It is also what the island needs.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The incident will be properly handled, and my ruling stays unchanged.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I expect your words to be matched by actions, Ms. Arcana.
His tone is cold, leaving no room for negotiation.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Certainly. It was a fair and just decision,

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: if only one could depart amidst such unfavorable weather.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I presume Ms. Vertin will also appreciate more time to prepare for the journey, what sayest thou?
It is a reasonable request, and her expression is nothing but decent and sincere.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The hourglass empties in two hours. Please leave before that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you for your thoughtful consideration.
The decision is met with no further objection from the people.
6 puts away the hourglass and looks at the silent audience.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Lastly, I would like to share a story,

items.speaker: Six
items.text: to conclude today's meeting, and respond to Ms. Arcana's tale.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I am most honored.
The leader raises his hands and faces the people.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I, too, have heard the story of the first circle. But in my version, more followed.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The first of man were intimidated by the enormity of nature and constantly tried to defy and escape it.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Our ancestors, however, had the opposite reaction. They found solace in nature, which welcomed them with a nourishing embrace, sharing its vastness and sublimity without reservation.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It was the perfect harmony. The moment the circle ceased to represent confrontation and avoidance.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: As we bathed in Apollo's illumination and wandered the tranquil shores, our souls resonated, and we were lifted to a higher wisdom.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: This was how we conquered our fears, emerged from ignorance, and allowed ourselves to indulge on the essence and Forms.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: This was the rise of the "classic man."

items.speaker: Six
items.text: May you all be blessed with the courage for reconciliation, the determination for peace, and the devotion to nature—qualities no less noble than caution and defiance.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: You may all leave now.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Please, just a moment!
A clear voice rings across the hall, stopping 6 in his tracks.
Her robe flutters as she stands up on the high podium.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will fix our circle!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: 888 was right. I have enraged Apeiron. I am responsible.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will go back to the sacred place, pass Its test, and ask It to share the divine light of Gnosis, so we can learn the Truth about the essence.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will make up for what I've done, I promise!
6 turns around, his eyes meeting the gaze of the determined star.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It has been three hundred years since the last challenger had their success in the cave.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: 37, are you aware that we have other means to cleanse the island, even if you don't bring the matter to Apeiron?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes, I'm aware.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Then are you aware of the price you will pay, should you fail Its test?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes, I am.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Then you shall have my blessing.
He leaves, ignoring the murmurs of shock.
The gavel is thus brought down.
The long debate has finally come to an end.
TO BE CONTINUED…
